title: Severe psychological distress
reference: NASA Behavioral Health and Performance (BHP) Operational Guidelines: Acute Behavioral Crisis & De-escalation Protocol.

q1.text: Does the crew member express suicidal ideation, violent behavior, severe psychosis, or present an immediate danger to themselves, others, or vehicle controls?

i_safety.text: IMMEDIATE SAFETY INTERVENTION: Assign two crew members to stay with the individual continuously. Lock critical hatch and cockpit control panels. Safely stow sharp objects, medications, and tools.

q2.text: Is the crew member cooperative, calm enough to speak, and willing to discuss their acute distress or panic symptoms?

i_deescalate.text: Guided De-escalation: Escort individual to a private, quiet module. Utilize active listening, validate feelings without arguing, guide slow 4-7-8 breathing exercises, and reduce sensory stimuli.

t_deescalate.text: Provide supportive, unhurried presence for 15 minutes. Re-evaluate heart rate, anxiety level, and emotional stability.

q_post_deescalate.text: Following 15 minutes of guided relaxation, have acute anxiety, hyperventilation, and agitation visibly diminished?

i_stabilized.text: ACUTE PANIC SUBSIDING: Offer hydration; guide mindfulness audio track; schedule sleep rest period and duty task offloading.

i_persist_distress.text: PERSISTENT ACUTE DISTRESS: Contact Flight Surgeon for evaluation of oral anxiolytic (e.g. Lorazepam) from the emergency psychiatric kit.

i_give_space.text: Non-verbal de-escalation: Allow personal quiet space in crew quarters while maintaining unobtrusive sightline monitoring. Offer warm beverage and dim cabin lights.

end_monitor.text: Acute distress subsided. Facilitate private Earth communications uplink with family; schedule follow-up rest and task offloading.

end_escalate.text: BEHAVIORAL CRISIS ESCALATION: Initiate private high-priority teleconference with NASA Flight Psychologist and Flight Surgeon. Medical countermeasure protocol active.
